title: Holographic Krylov complexity in confining backgrounds: particle, string, and frames
authors: Jasper Nongmaithem, Deepak Kumar Kar, Ayush Kumar, Shreeya Rajesh Parab, David Dudal, Subhash Mahapatra
abstract: We investigate holographic Krylov complexity in bottom-up holographic QCD models describing the confined phase, using the recently proposed correspondence between the growth rate of Krylov complexity and the proper radial momentum of probes, such as particles and strings, falling in the bulk spacetime. As representative confining backgrounds, we consider two horizonless geometries, namely the dilaton-deformed AdS-soliton and the deformed thermal-AdS spacetime, both arising as solutions of an Einstein-dilaton gravity system. We find that the Krylov complexity associated with a massive particle exhibits qualitatively distinct behavior in these two backgrounds when analyzed in the Einstein frame. In the deformed AdS-soliton geometry, the complexity undergoes periodic oscillations, with both the oscillation period and amplitude depending on the parameters of the model. In contrast, in the deformed thermal-AdS geometry, the complexity grows exponentially at late times and does not display oscillatory behavior. We then investigate string dynamics in the string frame and find that the Krylov complexity exhibits oscillatory behavior in both confining backgrounds. This behavior is traced to the emergence of an additional turning point in the deep infrared of the string-frame geometry. Motivated by this observation, we further analyze massive-particle dynamics in the string frame, where we find qualitatively similar behavior in the two confining backgrounds. Our results demonstrate that the Krylov complexity of confined holographic systems depends sensitively on the choice of probe and frame, while also revealing a closer correspondence between the two confining geometries in the string-frame description.
summary: This work applies holographic Krylov complexity to model the confined phase of QCD using two distinct background geometries. By analyzing particle and string probes in both the Einstein and string frames, the authors show that complexity diagnostics are highly sensitive to the chosen physical description. The findings suggest that while the complexity depends on the probe and frame, the string-frame description unifies the behavior of the two confining models.
main_problem: The paper investigates holographic Krylov complexity in confining backgrounds to understand the dynamics of strongly interacting matter in the confined phase of QCD.
main_result: The complexity's behavior depends sensitively on the choice of probe (particle vs. string) and the gravitational frame (Einstein vs. string), though the string frame reveals a closer correspondence between the two confining geometries.
method: The study uses the correspondence linking the growth rate of Krylov complexity to the proper radial momentum of infalling probes (particles and strings) in curved spacetime.
model_or_system: The models are bottom-up holographic QCD descriptions using two specific confining backgrounds: the dilaton-deformed AdS-soliton and the deformed thermal-AdS spacetime, derived from an Einstein-dilaton gravity system.
key_observables: Krylov complexity, proper radial momentum, and the induced line element for probes.
important_parameters: Model parameters governing the deformations of the AdS-soliton and thermal-AdS geometries.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the holographic conjecture linking complexity growth to radial momentum, and specific approximations are made for particle dynamics (e.g., setting initial transverse momentum to zero).
paper_structure: The paper analyzes particle dynamics in the Einstein frame for both backgrounds, contrasting oscillatory behavior (AdS-soliton) with exponential growth (thermal-AdS). It then examines string dynamics and particle dynamics in the string frame, noting qualitative similarities and oscillatory behavior in both cases.
why_interesting: The concept of complexity as a diagnostic tool for quantum chaos and thermalization, applied here to strongly coupled gauge theories via holography, provides a powerful theoretical lens for understanding confinement dynamics.
